extracted.intended_audience: readers and creators interested in feminist satire, comedy writers, media/culture consumers
extracted.subtask_description: Producing satire aimed at feminist topics and the media's treatment of women, using headline-driven parody, advice columns, confessional pieces, and breaking-news formats for a digital audience. Emphasizes topicality, tone, and balancing political seriousness with humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mocking tone / incisor-sharp humor
rubrics_metrics.description: The site uses a mocking tone and 'incisor-sharp' humor to deliver satire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of homepage headlines show the biting style (e.g., “We’re Piercing My Baby’s Tongue. Here’s Why.”, “Dying Woman Finally Achieves Body Acceptance”, “How to Make Your Vagina Look More Like His Man Cave”). The tone should be sharply comic and unmistakably satirical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Satirize the media's portrayal of women
rubrics_metrics.description: Content should be a 'stinging satire of the media’s portrayal of women'—parodying mainstream women's magazines and style sites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target outlets and tropes from Vogue, Cosmopolitan, People, Refinery29, and other 'women’s and fashion magazines' by imitating their voice and framing to expose their messages about women.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parody beauty/self-help tropes
rubrics_metrics.description: Spin relentless self-help, beauty tips and 'how to' articles into satire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transform common gimmicky advice into comedic pieces (examples: “How to Give Fellatio Like a French Woman with Low Self-Esteem”, “How to Write From Your Heart So Your Professor Will Fuck You”, “6 Superfoods to Help Fight Isis”). Use the familiar form to highlight absurdity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adapt satire to the mainstreaming of feminism
rubrics_metrics.description: As mainstream outlets start 'taking feminism seriously', satire must adjust its targets and approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produce more stories that parody 'sad attempts' by magazines to be relevant in feminism and to co-opt the movement while still propagating the same harmful messages. Reassess targets as the media landscape changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target contradictions within feminism (including 'white feminism')
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim satire at problematic or naive strands within feminism—e.g., 'white feminism' and lack of intersectionality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critique blind spots such as failing to acknowledge race, class, and gender-intersectionality while avoiding simplistic piling-on. Use satire to reveal contradictions in activists' behavior as well as in mainstream discourse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be self-critical / avoid demonizing individuals
rubrics_metrics.description: Make fun of yourselves as much as you make fun of others; prefer teaching moments to demonization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The piece cites the site's stance around Patricia Arquette: rather than demonize her, use the moment constructively. Avoid punching down or merely piling on; balance critique with an opportunity to educate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mine social media and 'knee-jerk' reactions for material
rubrics_metrics.description: Find a 'wealth of material' in reactionary feminism on social media and in hot takes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor Twitter and activist hot takes for 'knee-jerk' moments to satirize, but be aware of the pace and volatility of those conversations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use diverse satirical formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ multiple comedic formats—advice columns, confessional essays, breaking news stories, live shows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include advice pieces (“How to Make a Man-Friendly #YesAllWomen Post.”), confessional essays (“I LIVED IT: I Lost 20 Pounds By Running After People Holding the Door Open”), and fake breaking news. Variety helps hit different comedic beats and audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and click-friendly production pressure
rubrics_metrics.description: Operate under pressure to produce quick, attention-getting content due to the speed of online media ('Twitter slot-machine and news alerts').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge that many writers' first inclination is to be angry and blog; guard against producing emotional, low-quality pieces just to be first. Balance speed with craft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance political seriousness with humor
rubrics_metrics.description: Use satire to temper 'gloom and doom' on serious issues (e.g., anti-abortion laws, equal-pay timelines) without trivializing them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reductress 'pops up' to relieve bleakness with humor ('Next Level Braids To Earn the Workplace Respect You Deserve'). Ensure jokes acknowledge the gravity of underlying issues while providing comic relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize comedic quality over shock/offensiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish between genuinely offensive content and jokes that are 'simply unfunny'; aim for the latter to be funny, not just provocative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The founders note that many alleged 'offensive' jokes are not offensive—merely bad. Focus on craft so that provocation serves a joke, not the other way around.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain original editorial vision while expanding
rubrics_metrics.description: Grow the brand without losing the original voice and mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As Reductress expands into video and live shows, they stress 'trying to grow but not lose sight of our original vision and constantly hit that as hard as possible.' New formats must preserve core identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience targeting and expansion
rubrics_metrics.description: Know your current audience (majority in large cities) but aim to broaden reach into smaller markets via social media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan content to 'capture the hearts of all Americans'—i.e., craft pieces that resonate both with urban core readers and wider audiences as social followings grow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid overreliance on 'low-hanging fruit' like body image
rubrics_metrics.description: Body image is commonly targeted ('low-hanging fruit'), but overusing it can be repetitive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While body-image satire is effective, seek fresh angles and avoid an overdependence on the easiest targets to keep satire sharp.

rubrics_metrics.name: Craft parody headlines that mimic magazine voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Create headline-driven satire that closely imitates the phrasing and framing of the outlets being parodied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site's headlines deliberately echo magazine-style leads and clickbait structure (see opening headline examples). Mastering voice and headline mechanics is key to the parody's impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider production trade-offs among formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether new formats (video, live shows) are worth the resource investment relative to payoff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Founders report video 'isn't worth the payoff' yet and are instead focusing on site growth and comedy shows. Prioritize channels that give best return for effort without diluting content quality.
